name: NAR Genomics and Bioinformatics
fits_reason: A Methods Paper must 'include benchmarks against an adequate number of relevant alternative state of the art technologies' showing statistically significant improvement, on third-party benchmarks where they exist, and show suitability for large-scale computing (HPC or cloud). An Application Note (at most 3,000 words, 3 figures or tables) is meant for software, and there these benchmarks are only encouraged. The manuscript meets part of it: Section 4.2 benchmarks against one alternative tool, PLINK2, and shows neither a statistically significant improvement over several state-of-the-art tools nor large-scale (HPC or cloud) use, which a Methods Paper needs. As an Application Note the benchmarks are only encouraged, but the paper would have to be cut to 3,000 words and three figures or tables. Every novel bioinformatics component must be open source; code goes on GitHub and is archived in Zenodo before acceptance under an OSI-recognised licence (or the paper is not reviewed), with simple commands that deploy it on the reference datasets; a web service stays up for two years without registration. These rules 'will be strictly enforced'. The manuscript meets it: Code Availability: the code is on GitHub under OSI licences (AGPL-3.0 and MIT) and runs with two commands (uv sync, uv run start) or as a container. The Zenodo archive is due before acceptance, with the other archiving.
